executive_assessment.text: Named basin, grassland and Loess Plateau findings identify differentiated physical and production vulnerabilities, using dated national-communication evidence and modeled future water risks.
Recent disaster records provide named Shaanxi, Hunan and southern-province examples; national person-times and relocations must not be treated as unique-person or permanent-displacement counts.

Government reports describe warning, evacuation and adaptation-planning capacities, including village examples and checks for older, disabled and non-local residents. Selected successes do not establish representative effectiveness.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2018-12 reports: The communication identifies the Loess Plateau as China's most agriculturally vulnerable area; observed yield reductions affected one crop type on 90% and two types on 55% of its arable land.
Source dated 2018-12 reports: Warming and drying reduced northern-grassland forage yield and capacity, most in central-eastern Inner Mongolia and southeastern Gansu.
Source dated 2018-12 reports: By mid-century, water vulnerability is projected to intensify in Haihe, Yellow, Huaihe and Song-Liao basins under combined climate change and rising demand.

Source dated 2025-06 reports: MEE reports 2024 national precipitation 9% above the 1991–2020 norm; Yangtze-Huaihe Meiyu rainfall exceeded normal by over 50%, and North China rainy-season precipitation by 83%.

The ministry's 2024 progress report describes Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau coordination and research and reports 333.8 hectares of additional greening around Yellow River-area rivers, canals, lakes and reservoirs. These are government-reported activities, not independently evaluated resilience outcomes.

The 2024 disaster bulletin reports national flood/geological-disaster person-time impacts and emergency relocations, with deadly July events in Shaanxi's Shangluo/Baoji and Hunan's Chenzhou/Hengyang. Administrative counts are not unique-person prevalence or climate-attributable losses.

Source dated 2025-01-17 reports: Super Typhoon Yagi affected Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi and Yunnan in September 2024, causing four deaths and 189,000 collapsed or damaged houses, with reported direct losses of 72.03 billion yuan.

Source dated 2025-06-06 reports: In Tunshang Village, Zima Township, Qinglong County, Guizhou, warning and joint inspections led to 180 people moving from a landslide-risk area; 53 houses were damaged, with no deaths.

The ministry's selected Yangjiawan/Huangzhou case describes detection of levee seepage and emergency control works. Its estimates of people and farmland protected are reported counterfactual exposure estimates, not independently measured avoided losses.

Source dated 2025-06-06 reports: Before August 2024 storms, Pinggu District responders checked households including older, infirm, disabled and non-local residents in Tawa Village; 257 people were relocated from flood and landslide risk.

known_gaps.text: CHN is not listed in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json, and no countries/CHN baseline directory exists in this worktree; this extraction therefore has no pre-existing China dossier to extend.

No inspected China-specific primary source explicitly links climate hazards to FCV violence or conflict, or conflict insecurity to adaptation interruption; these links remain unsubstantiated rather than assumed absent.

The most geographically detailed national climate vulnerability assessment is the 2018 Third National Communication, an unofficial English translation using dated underlying studies; projected risks should not be read as current measurements.

National disaster totals and selected successful-response cases are government-reported; climate attribution, household-level vulnerability for most locations and independent outcome evaluation were not available in the inspected sources.
No verified country-specific climate-to-violence or reverse-FCV pathway was found; this is a search limitation, not proof of absence.
Older vulnerability findings use a 2018 communication and dated underlying studies. An undated cryosphere projection was excluded.
Disaster person-times and emergency relocations are not necessarily unique individuals or permanent displacement. Annual administrative totals combine hazards without anthropogenic attribution.
Ministry-selected successful cases and adaptation progress reports are official accounts without representative or independent outcome evaluation.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
